title: Open structural adjunction with normalized composite counit
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $1\le m\le n$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F_{Y,R}=Ra_{Y,R!}\dashv G_{Y,R}=a_{Y,R}^{\times}$, $\omega_{Y,R}=G_{Y,R}R_s$, and $\varepsilon_{Y,R}:F_{Y,R}\omega_{Y,R}\to R_s$, for $R=A,B$, on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $T_Y=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and denote the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison by $c_{Y,K}:T_sF_{Y,A}K\to F_{Y,B}T_YK$ [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Here bounded constructible finite-Tor means constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, and integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an affine open subscheme. It is a quasi-compact separated etale morphism of finite type. The open compact-support candidate for $U\xrightarrow jY\xrightarrow{1}Y$ is exact termwise $j_{!,R}$, left adjoint to $j^*$, with evaluation counit $e_{R,W}:j_{!,R}j^*W\to W$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. There are canonical counit-preserving identifications
$$j^*\omega_{Y,R}\cong\omega_{U,R},\qquad F_{U,R}\cong F_{Y,R}j_{!,R},$$
and, using these identifications,
$$\varepsilon_{U,R}=\varepsilon_{Y,R}\circ F_{Y,R}(e_{R,\omega_{Y,R}}).$$
For bounded-below inputs the identifications are the ones induced by the ordinary etale structural adjunctions and the canonical compact-support compositor [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]; thus the evaluation counit in this formula is the specified one. There is also the canonical coefficient-tensor identification $j^*T_Y\cong T_Uj^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

proof.text: Obtain local Noetherianity of Y from finite type over Spec k, and compactness from quasi-compactness of its structural morphism. Restriction to the affine open U gives local Noetherianity, while affineness gives compactness. Thus U and Y are Noetherian. Mathlib instances give quasi-compactness of j (compact source and quasi-separated target), separatedness, etaleness and local finite type. Nagata gives compactifications of aY and j followed by aY; the open immersion has its standard compactification.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q65-98e8dbd40 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX: two repairable faults, both repaired in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-dualizing-open-adjoint.json.

Background: the item is the open-adjoint node split off by O4's re-split of lem-coef-finite-dualizing (old steps 20-21). Live and side-live still have it unsplit with the same statement, so this delivery is not superseded. It creates no new nodes, adds no cycle (I checked reachability from every cited node, the added ones included) and cites no SGA. It follows main-20261015 lem-coef-finite-dualizing proof paragraph 2, the locality sentence. I checked Stacks 07A4, 0G7E and 0DV0.

What holds: the main argument is correct. The composite counit d=ε_Y∘F(e_G) matches def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction. Moving F_U⊣G_U across along β gives the counit ε_U∘β. det-sp-unique-right-adjoint then gives θ with ε_U∘β∘FJ(θ)=d, and at R_s this is exactly the stated formula. β=α_{a_Y,j}∘F(n^{-1}) has the right types. Restricting to bounded-below inputs uses the last clause of the unbounded-comparisons node.

Fault 1 (C1/E1): the statement asserts 'j is a quasi-compact separated etale morphism of finite type', but the delivered proof assumes it as given. It also takes Noetherianity of Y and U and compactifiability of a_Y, a_U and j for granted. These are needed for adjoint-locality, the compact-support normalization and the unbounded compositor. Old step 20 proved them and the delivery dropped that argument. Repair: a new Step 1 citing pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft, pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth, lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale, lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated (affine∩affine is quasi-compact, so j is quasi-compact), lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type and def-asd-compactifiable, with (j,1_Y) as the compactification of j.

Fault 2 (E5): Step 5 argued 'B-linearity follows since the comparison preserves the B action'. That is not a proof: the cited lemma works over the one ring A, and commuting with the B-action in D(A) does not give an isomorphism of B-complexes. Repair: a chain-level argument. Take a K-flat resolution P→K with flat terms. j^*P is K-flat (lemma clause), and restriction commutes with tensor products, so j^*(P⊗_A B_Y)=j^*P⊗_A B_U as B_U-complexes, naturally in K. No flatness of A→B is used.

Steps were renumbered (6 steps), cross-references updated and proof_deps recomputed. Statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged.

Edge cases checked: U empty, U=Y, m=n, unbounded K.
